notes.title: So. 2026. 10 years, huh?

But.

Next year is our 10th year of not going out of business, and we would really love to do *something*. Some sort of 10th Anniversary Edition of some game - obviously, with new stuff. New story. notes.content:
[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/33017070/f0773cdde99c1f4a89213af6fe6643c6c85ccade.jpg[/img]

[b]Happy May 12th, everybody! [/b] Yes, it is another sale. Yes, it is not April, when Shakespeare's birthday actually is. That was going to be the first of two things, but I started writing before I made the list, so here we are.

[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/33017070/8b396e5c5f64323c7346a9181402a495601e809e.png[/img]

Ten year ago, [b]Army of Tentacles 1[/b] was greenlit. A year after that, we had sold over 400 copies on Steam. Eight years ago, we decided to make every Shakespeare play into a game. We're two games away from that goal.

So, come one, come all, and peruse our fine (90%) anthropomorphic wares. It's what the Bard would have wanted. No, seriously, Shakespeare probably would be writing a furry webcomic.

[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/33017070/90a23201019a33da05b4a23794a6193eb4fca029.png[/img]

It's ALSO the Critter Collector Fest right now on Steam, and so that means.... well, it really just means another game on sale. But WHAT A GAME IT IS. 

A full-blown feline battle academy set in a San Francisco ravaged by tech lords (ok, so....), all legally distinct from the most popular creature collector out there!

[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/33017070/1b34f23748334c1d36ff63f30e381c7b201aa268.png[/img]

So. Time to talk turkey. 

[b]Army of Tentacles: Assault on Rainbow Unicorn Island[/b] is going to come out next Tuesday.

This game in no way should have taken as long as it did to come out. But that's the life of an indie dev company, especially if you want full VO in your game. 

The game's VO will be patched in at a later date. We already lost one backup of the VO files, and now the secondary may very well perish in the San Diego fires.

I'd rather not worry about video game bullshit right now. I'd rather focus on making sure my team is safe and not burning to cinders, or wondering where they are going to live in a few days. I'd rather they focus on that. Hell, they would rather they focus on that.

So, VO will be patched in at a later date.

notes.title: AoT: Unicorns = Halloween 2024? Spooky Cat Girls 2 = Halloween 2025?
notes.content:
[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/33017070/49ea5eb7e0e593edcb0495724de2d5a9fd62910c.jpg[/img]

Without going into my personal junk, about five to six life events hit me at the end of last year, one of which I had been prepping for. I/We already had decided to only work on Dinosaur Cousin Squad until it was ready for internal beta testers (which should be in the next few weeks), but with everything else that hit, it left me very emotionally drained. That and then you add in the Brain Fog, a loving reminder of my two bouts with COVID-19. 

The point is that I'm thinking of moving [b]Spooky Cat Girls 2[/b] to later, if not Halloween 2025. [b]Army of Tentacles: Assault on Unicorn Island[/b], if not out by then, would take its place as the Halloween 2024 game. I do not think there is any reason other than current lethargy that [b]AoT: Unicorns[/b] would land on Halloween 2024. 

[b]Cat Girls: IMT[/b] is looking good, but as stated, [b]DCS[/b] takes priority, and even if we barreled through it before SDCC in late July, we still wouldn't feel comfortable releasing it until at least December, if not later (for personal reasons as well as wishlists). 

We might do some weird, smaller game after [b]DCS[/b] level rough draft is done but before SDCC. [b]AoT: Christmas Edition[/b] has been thrown around just cause we were playing Lemmings: Christmas Edition last night. It would probably use the remaining art for Tentacle Prawn that we just never ended up using.

notes.title: Announcing the 2/4 Final Shakes Games!
notes.content:
[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/33017070/02a5f8c562f20acc023c1a5d56ae25ee7566f9d0.jpg[/img]
While progress on [b]Dinosaur Cousin Squad[/b] is going well (despite hitting an error as soon as we booted up the base code for the first time as one complete package), we were able to at least get a good foothold on two of the final four Paper Shakespeare games while waiting on the base code. We are very happy to be able to share the store pages with you today:

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2762590/Furry_Shakespeare_To_Date_Or_Not_To_Date_Cat_Girls_If_Made_Today
https://store.steampowered.com/app/2757940/Furry_Shakespeare_To_Date_Or_Not_To_Date_Spooky_Cat_Girls_2

[b]Cat Girls? If Made Today[/b] isn't a remake, but rather, a reimagining of the game if it was made with the game dev know-how that we have now, and with the storytelling and gameplay that we want to do. This is the first Cat Girls game as if it was completely unconnected to the other games, as the Keegan Quinn/Multiverse BS storyline is over. 

[b]Spooky Cat Girls 2?![/b] is another experimental title: it is three spooky games in one. The first is the titular Spooky Cat Girls, the second is a Cthulhu Dating Sim that we've been calling the Dark Souls of Visual Novels, and the third is our Kaiju game. 

Neither have solid dates yet, as we need to both launch [b]Army of Tentacles: Assault on Rainbow Unicorn Island[/b], as well as dedicate our time to finishing up Dinosaur Cousin Squad in time for Christmas - or before.

We hope you enjoy.

notes.title: The FINAL FIVE SHAKESPEARE + DCS update!
notes.content:
[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/33017070/a3690f55b8af0f5dccbcfd45c9c724daf41ba655.gif[/img]
The mad quest to make a game for every Shakespeare play is swiftly reaching its promised end, with the first being Army of Tentacles: [b]Assault on Rainbow Unicorn Island[/b]. After that, maybe we can sleep. 

Two are scheduled for the end of 2024, but the majority of work on those will commence after [b]Dinosaur Cousin Squad[/b] has dropped. We don't yet know when that one will have a Store Page up, but we assume within the next few months. Both games were being prepped while Dinosaur Cousin Squad was being worked on, but DCS progress has hit a few fun new snags, so we might be able to finish before proper level clean-up is set to begin in a few months. 

The final two are set for early and late 2025. One is a collaboration, and the other is another new engine, new genre game..... this time: a tRPG deck builder. In layman's terms, a party based tactical RPG with a card system. We've very recently begun pre-production and asset buy on that one. 

Store pages for at least two of the final four adaptations will be popping up after [b]Rainbow Unicorn Island[/b] drops on the 23rd.

notes.title: A note about AI art in our games.
notes.content:
So, for a few smaller games in the past (including tomorrow's Dinos Shakespeare 2 DLC), we have used AI backgrounds. We had both in-house discussions about it, as well as extensively made sure that the singular artist we used for said games was being ethical in what she fed her AI. 

[b]Scarecrows[/b] came out, and at the time, we assumed the generated art was made using the same level of care (as their prior art that we used from the same artist was painted), and while we have no reason to believe otherwise and do not wish to slander said artist, we will be working to attain new background art for [b]Scarecrows[/b]. This might look like a combination of new and existing art or it might be new art altogether. Regardless, it will not happen overnight.

We will not be using AI art of any kind in any future games. We apologize to both our fellow developers as well as our customers for any ill will gained via our actions.

[b]Army of Tentacles 1[/b]'s redo is about 50% complete. All of the side quests are finished. Brain fog is not helping my productivity, but I'm doing about two quests a day, plus a quest a day on [b]Army of Tentacles 2[/b]. 

I know I originally set the release date for February, and then March, but if they both are ready by the end of January, they might be both launching then.

Don't worry. I fully realize my workload as well as my current state of being/mind/health, so it might not happen.

[b]Army of Tentacles 3[/b] is a different story. It's a lot less restrictive than Army 1, both code-wise and VO-wise (because there is no VO). We thought about adding VO to the game, but ruled against it, as that would be money we need for [b]Unicorns[/b] and [b]Dinosaur Cousin Squad[/b], and the game's plot relied on a lack of VO. 

The biggest change to Army 3 is that we are cutting down the number of Arguments for a leaner, faster experience. With the DLCs, Army 3 has a whopping 70 Arguments to Army 1's, what, 20? I don't yet know how that is going to translate into quests yet. Some quests might be merged with others, I don't know yet. A lot of the Arguments were not even related to quests, and those may be the majority that go. Another feature that is going to take some busywork.... notes.title: Steam Winter Sale 2022! (+ Winter Updates)
notes.content:
[img]https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33017070/83e104259b3e54fb1c3293428e4574917d14fdef.png[/img]
[h1]Winter Sale[/h1]
No one could have predicted this.

Oh, and Dino Sim 2022 is droppig next week. Could be Monday, could be Friday. Or Tuesday. Or the other two. Just in time to miss Christmas as well as Christmas Eve. Blame the Gregorian Calendar and the constant shift of yearly dates for that chestnut.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2153400/Scientifically_Accurate_Dinosaur_Mating_Simulator_2022_American_Revolution_1775__1786
Oh, and a 2023 treat....

[img]https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33017070/121baf221805377562db7466bf68353786e9ab3e.jpg[/img]
[h1]Army 1 and 3: The Actual Recode(s)[/h1]
So, later on in 2023, the oft prophecized recode is happening..... the code for both Army 1 and Army 3 broke. The Steam versions still work. So that's the good news. If you buy it this sale, you will be buying a working game. It's just the versions on our end that need to be fixed. Which ultimately means that there will be a patch to both games later on down the line.

I want to make it clear that [b]both games work perfectly fine[/b] on Steam. If you were planning on making any purchases of the game or DLC this Winter Sale, feel free to do so.

When the newest update to the engine that we use hit, it scrambled our 2016 Code bases brain. Without going into lengthy explanations, the base code for Army 1 (Utahraptor) was written in such a way that, if you push one domino, the whole thing is gonna crumble. We were young and inexperienced. Shit happens.

While Army 3 came out pretty unscathed, it still uses the Argument/Word Battle code. So we need to redo it as well.

The good news is that both games will have fresher, better code. We will be keeping as much as the base game intact as we can. We're also going to try our best to keep the file size to the same as what it was, even though we'll be adding a few new baubles. They will include:
[list]
[*] [b]Updated Word Battles[/b]: Stats and abilities will now have a bigger impact on how they play out.
[*] [b]New Army Units and Art[/b]: We'll have actual art for the Army units.
[*] [b]New Level Up/Upgrade screens[/b]: For a better, clearer idea of how you're going to shape your army of monsters for the new endgame Invasion.
[*] [b]Updated [/b] Shops and Stats
[*] [b]Redone[/b] endgame Invasion system
[*] [b]Redone[/b] DLC pathcode
[*] [b]New[/b] UI
[/list]
Those patches will hit sometime (hopefully) early this year, with Army of Tentacles 1's patch going up before Army 3. 

[img]https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33017070/1cc95eb9870f83b93d977de5657b32941404430b.png[/img]
[h1]Introducing: DINOSAUR COUSIN SQUAD![/h1]
Our first platformer  - made in GameMaker Studio 2. While we were going to shift the release dates for our current 2023 crop to get this out before Summer Sale, the version of base code that we got earlier last month still needed a fair amount of polish, and we didn't want to have our contractors work through the holidays. Our current investors were cool with the shift, but since it's going to need more time to cook before we can really start work on it, we're going to try to clear our slate of current investor projects before working on this one in full. 

Earlier in October, we had split up into two teams: Team Army of Tentacles - working on Army 2, Tentacle Prawn, and Unicorn Island - and Team Cousin Squad - working on Dinosaur Cousin Squad only. But because Dinosaur Cousin Squad has shifted, Team DCS has now taken up a new project that will also be officially announced next month:
[img]https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33017070/5296b50d44424d80c3a3908b376abb9eb54ff686.jpg[/img]
[h1]To Date Or Not To Date Cat Girls? 2 is in development[/h1]
While [b]Tentacle Prawn[/b] is the game where we detail the relationship between our Lovecraft and Shakespeare worlds, [b]Furry Shakespeare: To Date Or Not To Date Cat Girls?[/b] 2 is going to be a more standalone title that deals specifically with the various Furry Shakespeare tales we've been telling so far. Do they also go to the same college for royalty that everyone else does? What about the Spooky Scary Halloween Spooky Times and Historylands crews? Those are retail jobs. Why do those exist in this world? 

But the most important question of all: can you date a Monarch Butterfly? 

Originally, [b]Spooky Cat Girls?[/b] was going to be the canon sequel to [b]Cat Girls?[/b], but.... well, not anymore, obviously.

notes.title: Kittens/SF: Maybe Delay
notes.content:
[b]First off, why the delay?[/b]

I finally got COVID-19.

The silver lining here is that most of the teams for the next few games already work remote, and [b]Kittens in SF[/b] is basically 98% finished. Which sounds relatively easy, but I have never felt this lethargic and aimless with any other cold or flu that I've had the chance of catching. There are maybe fifteen minute windows where I feel good enough to work on the game, but then those pass and I can't even think straight. Even with those fifteen minute windows, my body is constantly fluctuating between extreme hot and extreme cold. 

I can't talk, I can't smell, and while I still retain my sense of taste, it's dull in most areas but extremely punctuated in others. It's super weird.

[b]But wait, it's not all doom and gloom![/b]

While the game may be delayed, it won't be delayed that long, as I'll be out of isolation next week and plugging away to get you, the general public, your yum-yums.

At the very least, I'll probably take this time to finish up work on some future store pages so we can announce some new products in the interim. Who knows.

If you can, please get vaccinated. I have a mild case, but knowing it is a mild case, I would not want anyone to experience a full-on case of COVID. Because I can't even begin to imagine what that feels like. I also am still deep in recovery from a prior surgery, so these two factors combined are..... not great.

notes.title: Army of Tentacles 2022, Spooky Cat Girls?: Changes
notes.content:
[img]https://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33017070/093609f034bbf0c064c59ab751c2d65d3de347b5.png[/img]

Doing things isn't easy. 
Video games are hard, as someone once said I forget who, but it's an actual quote. I think it may be from an executive. I dunno.

Being a niche indie company is hard.

Hired a new writer for [b]Spooky Cat Girls?[/b]'s classroom scenes when it became clear that it would not make a reasonable launch date for October. It was either launch directly before the Halloween sale (and this was hoping Valve would accept the final build on the first submission, never something a designer should bet on) or delay it, and we chose to delay it. We feel December also fits in with the theme of the chosen play.

[b]Super Army of Tentacles[/b] has always been my baby, but it's gone through so many changes, due to gameplay as well as personal reasons, that I feel a disconnect with it. Rather than make a tentpole game that I do not want to make, I handed it off to another team member for a 2023 release. This would be the first Army of Tentacles game not helmed by me, which is exciting as I 100% trust my team and think it is time that we all grow in that fashion. We've been alive almost five-point-something years now.

In the place of [b]Super Army of Tentacles[/b], I plan on making a new, full VN-RPG Army of Tentacles game. I feel much more confident about this one, and it will launch at the same time that [b]Super Army 2022[/b] would have. That will be announced soon, maybe with the other 2022 games. Maybe not. Who knows.

Making games is hard.

notes.title: Super Army of Tentacles, progress update + news
notes.content:
So. 
Dunno if this announcement is really warranted. Just want to let people know what is going on. 

[b]Super Army of Tentacles: (Not) A Cthulhu Dating Sim[/b] has three main mechanics: skills/attributes, Word Battles, and Armies.

Well, it did. See, I started work on the project when things were.... let's say, different in the USA, and that, in turn, fueled the direction of the thing. We had already wanted to do something new with AoT 1's army mechanic, but do it better than the first game. Do it with all the game dev we had learned over the years since we've started. So I felt that my internal anger was a good fuel for said mechanic. Who doesn't love a good 'throw out the bad guys' story?

While the main story of the game is still 'the humans somehow occupied Monster Land', after recent events, I just don't feel good about a mechanic where you pre-meditatively build up militias to take over areas. We talked about this, and the bottom line is that we feel that even though the Army mechanic would have been solid, it would have taken away from the main gameplay loop of the first two games. Even though there was a final Invasion mechanic in the first game, the way you recruited your army was never the focal point. The focals were the Word Battles. 

At the end of the day, real people make games, and we don't want to be making a game that we feel isn't up to snuff or is pushed in two different directions. This is the last in the trilogy for us. We know more now and want to do it right, as both a stand alone title and a series cap.

This also allows us to put greater focus on the idea of reactivity to your choices in the world's hubs. Which is cool. 

I'm writing this because, even though it wasn't the selling point of the game or even showcased in screenshots or the trailer, it was in the initial store description and there were shots of it in the trailer and on the screenshot gallery. We've already updated the gallery, but will also be updating the trailer shortly. 

This really doesn't affect the already delayed release date of 2022. If anything, it clarifies a release date. If anything, at max what it means is this will release post-summer 2022, but I honestly don't think that's a concern.

notes.title: 2021 release date changes
notes.content:
[img]https://cdn.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33017070/7b1984b13272b203c42ad2527a8c027213b40964.jpg[/img]

[b]Furries & Scalies & Bears OH MY! 2[/b] has been moved so that it is launching either closer to or directly after [b]Super Army of Tentacles: (Not) A Cthulhu Dating Sim[/b].

[img]https://cdn.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33017070/67c3c6865ee2c45e187970d30a3e13ebefede1f4.jpg[/img]

One half of the reasoning behind this is because we wanted to give it more time to cook, and we had a much clearer vision for the two Furry Shakespeare games that were going to be our post-Army of Tentacles Winter 2021 games.

One of which is [b]To Date or Not to Date Cat Girls? 2[/b]. The other is one that we had been talking about since 2016 and are all very excited about. We just didn't know what it [i]was[/i] until now. We couldn't see it.

As these are games for an investor, we wanted to knock them out as soon and efficiently as possible while still launching good games. It's also that the Furry/Paper Shakespeare series has generally been more profitable than Furries & Scalies, so that's another reason. Had we all the time and money in the world, all three would be coming out before summer 2021, but that workload would eventually hurt Army of Tentacles 2021. notes.title: AoT Upgrade News, 6/30/2020 - end of line?
notes.content:
Okay, so here's the deal:

The Army of Tentacles 1 remaster is hitting some snags. The easiest to work on right now is that it is getting way too big file size-wise - bigger than the original size by far. So I don't think it is fair to drastically change the file size for an existing userbase. Which leaves the project with three options:

1) [b]Release it as a separate, free DLC instead of a free patch[/b]
But, if we're going to do this, we would have to throw in the new backgrounds as well (since there's absolutely no point in having DLC for DLC), and by then, we'd basically be selling the same game as a paid DLC. Which, while it is not unprecedented for a DLC to overhaul a base game's mechanics, it wouldn't serve the original purpose of the remasters, which was for every pre-exisiting and future user to have a retooled game.

2) [b]Only upgrade the resolution[/b]
This way, we'd still be able to sell the new backgrounds as an "HD 4K OMG LOLLERS" DLC for those that want a bit more of the game's backgrounds but still like the base game.

But that would potentially still increase the base game file size for existing users.

3) [b]Make a new Army of Tentacles game entirely, scrap the upgrade patches altogether[/b]
Obviously, if this happened, it would probably be the same price as the original game ($4.99) and use the art from either AoT 3 or [OTHER SECRET IN-UNIVERSE PROJECTS].

While this would be the easiest option, as of now, it's not the most ideal for us. 

[h2]Going forward...[/h2]
No idea what we are going to do yet, but we will let you know when we do have one.

Oh, and I feel like I'm getting sick. No, not COVID symptoms, more like weird stomach stuff.

I've got a schedule, but it is pretty tight, and when push comes to shove, it doesn't look good for the experiment known as Rainbow Hollow getting out anytime soon. I'm much more confident of getting Halloween Times out before summer, and even then, it is going to miss April completely for a May launch. Maybe. We'll see.

'RPG' was a fun title to give the game, and the new Argument System worked incredibly well with the Paper Shakespeare universe, but at the end of the day, we just couldn't figure out how to make it all fit together perfectly. notes.title: Argument System 3.0 and YOU!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11959844/47d2f23f1005f186cd14ce7beb36b3b1e57e04ef.jpg[/img]

We at the office have been working on the new foundation code for [b]Super Army of Tentacles: (Not) A Cthulhu Dating Sim[/b], and are so happy with its progress that we have decided to tear out the combat system for [b]Paper Shakespeare RPG[/b] and replace it with the new update to the Army of Tentacles series' Argument System. Honestly? It works better with the theme of the game, and means that we can get it out sooner.

We are still hard at work on a combat system for a later RPG. 

[h1]What will be included in the new system?[/h1]
A much more code-friendly system means that stats will greatly affect the word battles, as well as giving us the the opportunity to make much cooler skills that affect the battles in much deeper ways. 

[h1]Will you be putting Argument System 3.0 in the previous two Army of Tentacles games? Say, before the new Army of Tentacles comes out?[/h1]
I would love to say yes. Let's get into why it might not happen, or might take a while to happen.

Because of the way the original Utahraptor framework (the thing that holds all our systems together in RenPy) was written, it would require a complete code overhaul, and that means an overhaul of two separate games. In that case, we're basically redoing [b]Army of Tentacles: (Not) A Cthulhu Dating Sim[/b] and [b]Super Army of Tentacles 3: The Search for Army of Tentacles 2[/b] from the ground up. 

Even with an existing script to work off of, we're also talking all of the DLC, the works. Everything would be redone. Every scene, every quest, every Argument, every mechanic. Then we'd need to actually take the copy-pasted Argument System 3.0 and make sure it would have the things required for that specific game. 

We're also talking about doing this at no cost to the user, just a simple, free patch. Sadly, we have to weigh that in as a factor, as we do have other games on the slate. We're talking about a 2016 game and a 2017 game, after all. Would we improve the art and resolution for Army 1, to put it in line with the other two games in the trilogy? Would we do art but just leave the resolution the same? 

Is it unfair to any new or existing players to leave Army 1 and Army 3 as is if the new one is going to be, for lack of any other term, badass?

[h1]The Summary[/h1]
[b]Paper Shakespeare RPG[/b] is getting a cooler combat system. Dunno yet if the previous [b]Army of Tentacles[/b] game will get a facelift.

We're very excited to show you the next step.

notes.title: Anncouncing: clarification of COLLECTION BUNDLES.
notes.content:
As we are quickly approaching four games, we thought it best to clarify the categorization and order that our games will be bundled together by:

[h1]Army of Tentacles: Ultimate H.P. LOLcraft Deluxe Platinum Non-Award Winning Pack[/h1]

[h1]The Ancient Texts Pack[/h1]

Will include all games adapted from previous writings from members of our company. The two first included will be Joe Papp and Game 5 (which will be announced shortly after Paper Shakespeare's launch).

[h1]The 100% WAIFU Pack[/h1]

Will be all the dating sims. Yes, we said plural. 

[h1]Buy Every Game We've Ever Made (thank you)[/h1]

Will be every game we've ever made. No collections, no DLC, just every base version of every game that we have ever made. Obviously, everything that is not "counted" towards the previous lists ends up here.

[b]A note on packs:[/b] Each game that gets some sort of Ultimate Edition later on down the line will have that version replace the base version (along with all DLC for that game) in the bundle.

notes.title: A note on future discount sales.
notes.content:
I feel that we need to make an official announcement about this, lest people start going "hey, they said they were going to do X and aren't. Unreliable devs! Pitchforks!".

Originally, the plan was to always bundle the base versions of the Army games with the Black GOAT versions in any future discount sale, but after having both internal as well as external discussions, we feel that it is in everyone's best interest to keep them separate.

We honestly thought that people would want to have the option of both discounted products during the same sale, but found that it just ended up being really confusing. We also didn't/don't want to run the risk of someone buying the same exact product during a sale. 

It also comes down to choice: if someone is looking to buy Army 1 to test it out, they are going to buy Army 1, regardless of the price of the GOAT Edition. And if someone is going to refund one of our games based on a test run, it is really not in our best interest for it to be the higher priced one. Refunded DLC is much better than a refunded fully priced game. 

As for official Steam sales such as the Summer and Winter sales, both will be on sale at the same time.

[h1]WHAT'S UP FOR 2018?[/h1]

A few things. I'm not going to go into a bunch of medical mumbo jumbo, but it looks like I'm out of the woods in terms of a long recovery. That is as specific as I feel I need to be.

On to the fun stuff:

Right now, we're thinking of having Army 1: Black GOAT be the primary product to go on sale, and Army 1 Vanilla just won't.

[b]PROJECT RED NOTEBOOK[/b]: Just started formulating the team for that one. Would love to get it out alongside Updike, but time (and funds) will tell.

[b]HYPOTHETICAL D&D DLC FOR THE GHOST OF JOE PAPP[/b]: Again, this is up to funds. It would be by Halloween.

notes.title: Year Update: some medical chicanery.
notes.content:
Bryy here (I mean, it's always safe to assume that I'm the one writing these things because, 90% of the time, I am). Update on the rest of the year.

Earlier this morning, I ran into some medical issues - some old war wounds that decided they would like to wish me a late happy birthday. Nothing major, and even the definition of the surgery I need is minor. Which is a let-down, as I totally would have been cool with looking up the classification and finding that it just passes for MAJOR SURGERY. 

However, having had this surgery at least once in my lifetime, I can tell you that the recovery process is rather long and hard on the body. 

But on to the meat.
What does this mean for the rest of the year?
[list]
    [*][b]CHARITY DLC #3: DESERT BUS[/b]: Moved from this week to most likely next week due to doctor visits.
    [*][b]SPOOPY! SALE[/b]: Expect it to be moved to late this month and downsized to Army 3 only. There will still be an Army 1 sale in mid-October.
    [*][b]HALLOWEEN QUEST AND OUTFIT PACK[/b]: Still on track for October 13th.
    [*][b]NEW GAME+ BENEFITS 2 EXPANSION PACK[/b]: Depends on recovery. If the surgery is in November, expect NG+B2 in January. If December, expect February.
    [*][b]The Ghost of Joe Papp[/b]: Same as NG+B2. Depends on recovery. If the surgery is in November, expect Joe Papp in January. If December, expect February.
[/list]

notes.title: Discount mix-up: Birthday Sale Update
notes.content:
Well, so we got to the bottom of what happened to mix up the discount sale, and we're happy to announce that the Birthday Sale is still on.

A few compromises.

It is no longer a weekend-long flash sale of super low prices on all Army 1 items, but instead a regular two week discount sale of regular mark downs. 

Why? Two reasons: the first being that if we did a flash sale, it would knock all Army 1 items out of the running for the SPOOPY/Twitch Con sale in October; the second being that we still really wanted to do a sale that was around the time of significance for our team - namely birthdays. So we picked a date that would satisy both of these requirements. 

The Birthday Sale will run August 7th - 20th.

notes.title: SUPER ARMY 3 update!
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/11959844/12c7f1254b25ab297747024570d58130e9019ff4.jpg[/img]

Good news, everyone! We've been approved for Steam release! We're halfway done with the code, and the BETA is currently being played by a small group of awesome people! 

This morning, we just recieved the last background art for the Boston hub, so now we have the full art for one entire hub done. Speaking of hubs, since the last update, we've had to cut down the size of the world map in order to beef up the various hub locations.

The Middle East and most of Europe are gone, with their respective scenes going to the East and West Coast, respectively. While we wanted a globe-trotting adventure, we felt that, ultimately, we needed to focus less on size and more on scope. 

Argument System 2.0 should be up by this weekend, but will not be input into the code until next month. We're focusing 100% on finishing the main paths before we begin on that.

Our roadmap right now looks like this:

* FEBRUARY: Finish the main path of the game, playtesting various areas while we go.

* EARLY MARCH: Set up the Argument and Party Systems. Depending on how this goes, it might push our schedule back a bit. Playtesting.

* MID MARCH: Start creating the Arguments, of which we aim for around fifty for variety sake. We don't want people running into the same RNG Argument over and over. Playtesting.

* LATE MARCH: NPCs & Side Quests. While at least 90% of all dialogue NPCs are in-game and we have our dialogue and quest systems set up as well as a Quest Book, we are not focused on side quests or misc. dialogue at this point. Playtesting. 

* EARLY APRIL: Make sure everything is polished. Put up the Steam page.

* APRIL 24th - MAY 19th: Release window.

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/11959844/3e8ec1d11d95a9e3331290411fc7d3bd50d73612.jpg[/img]

As far as DLC goes, we'd love to have some sort of "NIGHT BEFORE SEQUEL" free DLC, but as of now, we have no idea what we would put in such a thing. All our Totally Not OP Items are already in our other DLCs.

We don't know how to make things more OP.

notes.title: Paper Shakespeare and Steam Greenlight
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/11959844/1759c47beb25cc441698ad403a7d764145169bfb.jpg[/img]

There has been discussion of pulling Paper Shakespeare: It's Hamlet (Again)! from Greenlight. This would be for a few reasons.

Whereas we are not that concerned with how long PS would potentially be on Greenlight, there has been internal discussion about taking what we've learned from both PS and Army 3 and putting it to work revamping Paper Shakespeare. It was always a much smaller project, not meant to be big, but we have had internal discussion regarding.... what if it could be? 

If it could be, then we of course should take it down. The product currently showcased on Greenlight would either be compromised at least and invalidated at worst. 

If it can't, then we at least can revamp the presentation. Clean up the description, add in some graphics, make a newer and more enticing trailer. 

A third variable: does having Paper Shakespeare as part of our official Steam library hurt or hinder our growth as a company? We don't want to put out a message that can be misinterpreted as apathy for "traditional product growth". We've always wanted to make bigger and better games while at the same time working on smaller projects to support us through growth spurts. 

We appreciate everyone's support so far. We don't want to seem ungrateful. If the project was past a point where we could easily do this, it wouldn't even be considered.

Now, I guess we'd like to ask you what you think of this.

Our decision ultimately probably will not be for a week or so.
